description.narrative: PSSD2 is a 2.5-year project aiming to support the scaling and industrialization of the Burundian seed industry and realize a mature and competitive industry that is capable of innovation and which, due to its business-friendly regulatory environment, vibrant private sector and strong consumer base, is an attractive partner to the international seed industry.The project’s implementation will be based on public and private approaches and will make its impact through the following components:- Component1: Continued Seed Sector Development: Scaling and Industrialization- Component2: Business Enabling Environment Strengthened- Component 3: Farmer Household Resilience Increased- Component 4: Mainstreaming of PSSD approaches in the Burundi Seed Sector policy, programs and projects funded and other projects and programsBy performing the activities designed under each component, the project will make its impact on: -64 500 small-scale food producers who progressively realize a living income-90 300 small-scale food producers who progressively decrease the yield gap-31 500 small-scale food producers whose livelihood became more resilient to shocks-31 500 small-scale food producers directly reached with activities aimed at structural/systemic improvement of their agricultural performance-189 000 small-scale food producers indirectly reached with activities aimed at structural/systemic improvement of their agricultural performance.The PSSD-2 design can best be understood when keeping in mind a number of seed sector development principles which the Project implementation principles the project adheres to:•A private sector driven seed sector, based on the strong foundation, laid by ISSD and PSSD, of many private seed entrepreneurs of different scales, from community-based to national scale, competing for the market. •Assure a system with direct relations between seed producers, seed traders and seed clients, to facilitate informal trust-based quality assurance•Brand building by private seed entrepreneurs, as the second component of trust-based quality assurance •Effective, affordable and rapid seed certification, as the third component of quality assurance•Facilitate private-public collaboration for sector innovation and governance•For food security impact and rural income increase, combine seed sector development with training of farmers on quality seed use and good agricultural practices•Focus on crops with a large domestic market and for which quality seed makes a difference in productivity and is commercially viable•Continued efforts to build a direct seed market, parallel to the aid and institutional marketThe long-term vision of the PSSD-2 for the Burundi seed sector is a seed industry:•Which serves the diverse demands of Burundian agricultural producers with access to quality seeds at an affordable price•Which adds value to the Burundian economy through the export of seeds based on an excellent reputation in the sub-region for high quality certified seeds•Which is driven by liberally competing, profitable and professional private companies, of different sizes and specializations•Which is supported by transparent, efficient and customer-oriented regulatory bodies and national seed policies •Which collaborates between actors with the objective of continuous innovation and the resolution of constraints

The global objectives of the intervention are to contribute to improved food security and income of small-scale producers (sphere of interest). These higher objectives are realized through increased farm productivity and associated with more competitive agricultural commodity prices (sphere of influence). With these global objectives, the project will lead to the following global change: -Resilient and food secure households with profitable surplus production -Affordable food for non-farming population-A professional seed industry creating added value, offering jobs and investment opportunities -A professional seed industry offering affordable quality seed to smallholder farmers Besides these global objectives, the project aims to achieve the following long et intermediate objectives as described below: long-term objectives:1.A dynamic private seed industry, serving the domestic market with added earnings from exports by intermediates objectives: 2.Seed Sector enabling environment safeguarding fair competition, rewarding quality and facilitating innovation 3.Resilient smallholder farming in which quality seed and adapted farming practices assure a sustainable living incomeIntermediate objectives: 1.1.Seed companies’ technical advancement and specialization 1.2.National market coverage with affordable high-quality seed 1.3.National and international Business to Business (B2B) collaboration 1.4.regional seed market penetration 2.1.An autonomous strong national seed federation (COPROSEBU) 2.2.A transparent early generation and institutional seed market 2.3.client oriented quality assurance and variety registration 2.4.private- public collaborative seed sector governance 3.1.Smallholder producers trained in quality seed use, sustainable climate smart farming and farming business3.2.Scaling approach for national impact tested, tried, documented and communicated Rapid distribution of cassava varieties with double mosaic and brown streak resistant National seed roadmap 4.National seed roadmap

The target group for projects is categorized into 2 categories:1° Direct beneficiaries which comprise of: -private seed producers with activities consisting of producing and selling certified seeds-farmers who will participate in demo plot on CEP (Champ Ecole Paysans) 2° Indirect farmers who will benefit from the project by buying certified seed from private seed producers subcontracted by the project or from other seed producers whose seeds have been certified by the National Office in charge of seed certification (ONCCS).
